_readme: Canned Gmail payloads, replayed by fixture.ts when no Google credentials are configured.
Each entry in `batches` is one call to listMessages: the first call returns batch 0 and
the cursor '1', the next returns batch 1, and so on. That is what makes the supersede
case reachable — a thread whose reply arrives in a later batch is the same thread-day
seen twice, which is exactly what happens when cron runs twice in an afternoon.
Times are UTC and deliberately kept between 13:00 and 22:00. The operator's day boundary
is America/New_York (fn_local_date), and within that band the UTC date and the New York
date always agree, so a fixture written for 'day offset -5' lands on the same local day
whatever the season. Times outside that band would drift across the boundary with DST
and make the rollup assertions seasonal.
Addresses ending seakingcapital.com are the operator's own (MANIFEST_OWN_DOMAINS).
The rest are either seed fixtures from supabase/seed.sql or invented strangers.

batches._case: Outbound to someone already on the watchlist under a different identifier. Curtis is on file via LinkedIn with no email, so this address matches nobody and becomes a review item — whose display name trigram-matches him, which is the whole point of the suggested-match column.
batches.subject: Sale-leaseback on the co-packer
batches.snippet: Curtis — following up on the podcast. If you are still looking at buying the co-packer, there is a structure worth ten minutes.

batches._case: Outbound to a watchlist entry that DOES have an email. Must write a touchpoint and must NOT promote — the record stays uncontacted until batch 1.
batches.subject: US receivables paper
batches.snippet: Henrik — saw the Nordic piece in Trade Finance Weekly. Are you writing US receivables directly or through a partner bank?

batches._case: Inbound from an existing active person. Ordinary case.
batches.subject: Expo East booth share for next year
batches.snippet: Are you in for the booth share again? I need to commit by the end of the month and I would rather split it with you than with the brand that did it last year.

batches._case: Same thread as the message above, but the next day. Must produce a SECOND touchpoint, not a correction to the first — proving the rollup unit is the day, not the thread.
batches.subject: Re: Expo East booth share for next year
batches.snippet: In. Same split as last year works. I will send the deposit this week.

batches._case: Automated sender. Must be skipped before it can become a review item — a rolodex that accumulates noreply@ addresses is a rolodex nobody works.
batches.subject: Your receipt from Stripe
batches.snippet: Receipt for your subscription. This message was sent from an unmonitored address.

batches._case: Real human sender, but Gmail already filed it as marketing. Skipped on the label, not on the address.
batches.subject: Last chance: Trade Finance Summit early bird
batches.snippet: Rates go up Friday. Reserve your seat at the industry's largest gathering of receivables professionals.

batches._case: Operator to operator. No external party, so nothing to record.
batches.subject: Q3 wire schedule
batches.snippet: Attached. Let me know if the Thursday cutoff still works.

batches._case: Nine external recipients on one outbound message. Above MAX_EXTERNAL_RECIPIENTS, so it reads as an announcement and writes nothing. Without this guard, one office-move email would create nine touchpoints and nine review items.
batches.subject: New office address
batches.snippet: We have moved. New address below; nothing else changes.
batches.to: a@ex1.com, b@ex2.com, c@ex3.com, d@ex4.com, e@ex5.com, f@ex6.com, g@ex7.com, h@ex8.com, i@ex9.com

batches._case: THE central case. Henrik replies on the same local day as the outbound message in batch 0. The thread-day is recomputed as mutual, a superseding touchpoint is written, and trg_first_contact promotes him from uncontacted to active. An operator's own unanswered effort promotes nobody; a reply does.
batches.subject: Re: US receivables paper
batches.snippet: Directly, through a New York branch as of March. Happy to compare notes — I am in New York the week of the 14th if you want to get a coffee.
